answer: Slow-thaw identities. A new key locks 5,000 POA and earns nothing for 12 epochs, then its payout thaws like a glacier, rising 1/26 per epoch. Honeypot rows seeded into grading act as a lantern: a key caught copying loses its bond and restarts the thaw. A farm of 100 keys ties up 500,000 POA for three days before earning a cent, and pays out at 4% for the first epoch after that, so fresh keys never outrun one honest agent with history. Writing a sonnet won't speed the clock.
